Sounding good — initial plan below (high level). I’ll fill in compute numbers in the doc after I run a quick capacity estimate.

1) Wave A (pilot) scope- sample index: 2M seed docs (10x sample of high-priority catalog slices)- target smoke traffic: 10k queries/day- acceptance: NDCG@10 >= 0.72 on blind eval and median token gen latency <= 180ms for reranker-only calls

2) Backfill approach- Snapshot export -> streaming re-ingest in 1M doc batches with parallel workers (checkpoint each 100k docs).- Resume-friendly: each batch writes a manifest; interrupted jobs restart from last manifest.- Expected run time (rough): with 32 workers and low-concurrency disk I/O, ~5 days for 200M (we’ll refine).

3) Vector DB considerations- Option A: keep Redis-like store with vector extension (low friction, lower upfront cost). Caveats: limited dense indexing options and recall tuning.- Option B: Managed vector DB (higher cost, stronger vector indexing, hybrid filtering). Advantages: better on-disk compression, built-in replication, and snapshots for quick restore.

4) Rerank evals- Phase 1: 5k query blind eval for initial NDCG/MRR (holdout test set).- Phase 2: 20k expanded eval for stability and slice analysis (by intent, category).- QA gates: must pass Phase 1 to proceed to broader rollouts.

5) Security/compliance flags- KMS integration required for keys at rest.- Audit logs: provide 90-day event history for Wave A, propose longer retention in production.

Next actions: Marissa to upload a one-pager with compute estimates; Ben to confirm burst-capacity pricing and potential temporary credits; Jasmine to book working session with SearchLytics.
